title: carmind vehicle knowledge base
description: Draft canonical schema. Facts mined from OEM owner's manuals. No user data. Every indicator, procedure and manufacturer-based drivability gate carries provenance.

drivability_dimension.description: The universal trio, judged to the legal/safety threshold, not perfection: brakes to legal standard / accelerates without engine damage / steers within safety law. e.g. vibration only at 60km/h+ = steering dimension, drivable, schedule tire center (not tow).

drivability_basis.description: Why the verdict holds. legal = Israeli roadworthiness law (vehicle-agnostic, no manual). manufacturer = manual-stated safety/damage. The fleet operator's commercial policy is not stored here; it layers on top and keys off damage_risk.

authority_ref.description: Provenance for basis=legal facts: points at a regulation, not a manual.

tire_provision.description: Car-type fact from manual. Resolves the spare gotcha: on inflation_kit/none_exempt cars a missing spare is EXPECTED, not a fault.

message_text.description: verbatim dash message if any, e.g. 'Stop immediately, service vehicle'

hard_stop.description: true = manufacturer hard stop (severity stop_now). Forces not_drivable and skips triage, so no field fix is attempted.

fleet_procedure.description: The fleet operator's own icon/symptom rulebook entry. It is their content: carmind hosts it and displays it first, attributed, but does not author or verify it. The manufacturer/legal assessment renders underneath as the deeper layer.

owner.description: marks this as authored by the fleet operator: displayed first, never mined or edited by carmind

context_flag.description: Per-car query-time inputs supplied by the fleet operator. Not stored by carmind: processed per request, never persisted. They modulate the decision; they are not car-type knowledge.

context_rule.description: Escalation modifier keyed on context flags (+ optional symptom). Expresses operator-risk judgment, e.g. 'repeat_problem -> tow, don't attempt field fix'. source=playbook (human-authored).

when_symptom.description: optional symptom_id this rule is scoped to; empty = any

then.description: raise_conservatism = flip ambiguous/default branches toward not-driving

triage_check.description: Runs BEFORE the fault tree. Cheap yes/no the operator asks to resolve non-faults (fob battery, door ajar, broken start sequence). source=playbook means human-authored, no manual page.

on_confirm.description: resolved = non-fault, stop here; continue = move to next check / fault tree

resolution_en.description: what to tell the customer if this resolves it

type.description: field_fix = dispatch operator to fix at roadside (lamp/wipers); schedule = route maintenance for later (near interval); tow = recommend tow (the fleet operator executes it). Multiple cheap field_fix + schedule can bundle on one drivable car.

ref.description: id of the procedure / drivability_gate / indicator this resolves to

question_en.description: what the operator asks the customer

discriminator.description: what this node is establishing, e.g. 'when does the wobble occur', 'sound character'

match_en.description: the answer this branch matches, e.g. 'high-pitched squeal'

default_branch.description: taken when the customer can't cleanly answer. On a high-liability tree this has to be conservative (escalate / not_drivable), never a 'probably fine' resolution.

diagnostic_tree.description: Branching diagnostic for symptoms that fork on discriminating questions (e.g. braking vibration). Distinct from the linear triage_check chain.

liability_tier.description: high = braking, steering, anything where a wrong 'fine' is a safety call. Forces conservative default_branch + human sign-off.

signed_off.description: high-liability trees require explicit human sign-off before they can be served

drivability_gate.description: Safety-critical; needs a strict second-pass verification. Three independent axes: legal roadworthiness, manufacturer/mechanical safety, and damage_risk (the hook the fleet operator's commercial tow policy keys off; that policy itself is not stored here).

vehicle_scope.description: empty = applies to all vehicles (typical for basis=legal)

condition.description: e.g. 'engine warning light + reduced power / limp mode' or 'broken mirror glass (reflective surface), housing alone does not qualify'

damage_risk.description: true = continued driving compounds the fault/repair cost even if the car physically moves. The hook the fleet operator's fleet-protection policy reads. Independent of legality.
